items.title: Suno faces investigation in Italy over terms of service
items.excerpt: Italy's competition watchdog AGCM opened an investigation into Suno's terms; concerns include price changes, account terminations, US-based arbitration, and a content licence it says requires users to waive moral rights over what they create.

items.title: Google picks Base for Music for its Gemini Startup Forum – as $1.7M-backed French company says it uses AI to predict music marketing ROI
items.excerpt: French music-tech firm Base for Music, selected for Google's Gemini Startup Forum, says its AI predicts the return on music marketing campaigns before money is spent. Borderline: AI-tool angle for label and artist marketing teams.

items.title: Fender revamps its website with AI tool and more artist content
items.excerpt: Fender has relaunched its website with an AI tool and more artist content. It's the latest step in a decade-long move beyond instruments into music education, its Fender Studio software and other digital services.

items.title: ARIA boss warns Australian politicians on AI lobbying demands
items.excerpt: ARIA's chief warned Australian politicians about AI companies' lobbying demands. Australia is one of the countries where the music industry is fighting tech firms for lawmakers' attention as AI rules are being weighed.

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.excerpt: Two rulings matter for AI music this week: a Japanese court held that publicity rights cover a performer's voice, and a US appeals court in Thomson Reuters v Ross found that copying data to train an AI was not fair use.

items.title: YouTube Shorts Recommendations Will Prioritize 'Genuinely Valuable' Original Content
items.excerpt: YouTube has changed the Shorts algorithm to 'focus on originality', pushing down repetitive and low-effort mass-produced uploads, which affects AI-generated music and remix content on the platform.

items.title: Introducing Eleven v4, our most emotive model
items.excerpt: ElevenLabs launched Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo with more emotional nuance, faster responses and stronger voice cloning, live in ElevenAgents, ElevenCreative and the API. It's free for a limited period, and it makes vocal and voice-performance work easier to direct.

items.title: The Search: Make the World's Catchiest Ad | $100,000 Competition
items.excerpt: ElevenLabs launched The Search, a global contest to make a 15-45 second ad for a fictional brand with an original jingle made in ElevenCreative. It offers $100,000 in prizes across 11 winners, with a $50,000 grand prize.

items.title: The next music economy will run on autonomous AI agents
items.excerpt: An op-ed arguing that autonomous AI agents, with human oversight, could fix music's fragmented rights, metadata and royalty systems and help companies pay creators faster.

items.title: 참가자도 심사위원도 AI…中 오디션, 재미의 공식이 달라졌다 [유화연의 차이나뷰] ②
items.excerpt: China has brought AI into the audition show itself: human singers and AI compete on the same stage, and AI also sits on the judging panel, which changes how music entertainment formats work.

items.title: Watch what Herbie Hancock had to say about technology in 1984
items.excerpt: CDM revisits a 1984 film of Herbie Hancock with Quincy Jones and the Fairlight CMI, reading it against today's AI debate: musicians who want to get better should look for cognition and practice, not AI or a new preset.
